criterion_notes.c1: Examines compound-level and household piped water and sewer-connected pour-flush sanitation service access, disconnection, reconnection, working connections, main water sources, and consumption in Nairobi's informal settlements.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, it evaluates utility governance and enforcement interventions. Under the narrow rule-type reading, although the first experimental arm (tenant face-to-face engagement) is behavioural/outreach promotion, the second experimental arm directly tests systematic contract enforcement of utility service disconnection and cost-recovery rules for arrears—including stricter arrears eligibility screening, formal disconnection notices, financial hardship exemptions/flexible payment plan accommodations, physical service disconnection, and reconnection rules directly governing water and sanitation access.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary quantitative empirical evidence from two randomized field experiments (an individual-level RCT on 2,584 accounts and a two-stage street-cluster RCT across 147 clusters / 3,253 accounts, with 1,001 disconnection-eligible compounds) linked to five years of daily utility billing records and baseline/endline surveys of property owners and tenants.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports multiple service access and affordability outcomes (physical disconnections and reconnections, compound piped water connection, sewer-connected pour-flush toilet, working piped water connection, piped water as main source, metered piped water consumption, monthly household water expenditure, and weekly water-fetching time). Null endline effects on connection rates do not affect eligibility.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (compounds, property owners, and tenant households in Nairobi informal settlements), exposures (tenant payment engagement vs. targeted contract enforcement of disconnection rules with hardship accommodation), outcomes (payment, disconnection/reconnection, water/sanitation connection and functionality, consumption, expenditure, time fetching water, rental market outcomes), and study design (individual and two-stage cluster RCTs) are all clearly specified.

evidence_quotes.quote: We estimate the impacts of two interventions implemented as field experiments in informal settlements by Nairobi’s water and sanitation utility to improve revenue collection efficiency and last mile connection loan repayment: (i) face-to-face engagement between utility staff and customers to encourage payment and (ii) contract enforcement for service disconnection due to nonpayment in the form of transparent and credible disconnection notices.

The second approach was to systematically enforce the terms of the contract that the property owners had signed with the utility, specifying service disconnection for property owners with signiﬁcant payment arrears.
If property owners were found to be indigent and/or agreed to a ﬂexible payment plan, they would not be disconnected.
We then randomized 73 clusters consisting of 1,584 accounts into the treatment group, while the remaining 74 clusters (1,669 accounts) were left as pure controls.

whether the compound had a pour-ﬂush toilet and piped water connection at the time of the endline, whether the water connection was working, the main source of water used by compound residents, the amount of time spent fetching water in the last week, the amount spent on water in the last month, and the overall piped water consumption in the compound.

The enforcement intervention had little eﬀect on compound connections to water and sanitation services. The majority of the 96 disconnected compounds were reconnected after agreeing to pay a portion of their balance.

raw_response.exposure: Two utility interventions in compounds with payment arrears: (1) face-to-face outreach engagement with tenants to encourage landlord bill/loan payment, and (2) systematic contract enforcement of utility disconnection rules for nonpayment (stricter arrears eligibility threshold, five-step transparent disconnection notice protocol, financial hardship appeal / flexible payment plan accommodation, and physical disconnection/reconnection).
raw_response.outcome: Utility bill and connection loan repayment (payment incidence, total amount paid, share of balance paid), physical service disconnection and reconnection, compound piped water connection, pour-flush sewer toilet connection, working piped water connection, piped water as main household source, metered piped water consumption, monthly household water expenditure, weekly water-fetching time, service fairness/quality perceptions, tenant mental well-being, and compound rental income/tenancy.
raw_response.population_and_sample: Compounds, property owners, and tenant households connected to municipal piped water and sewer services in informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya (2,584 tenant compounds in the engagement RCT across 6 settlements; 3,253 compound accounts in 147 street clusters across 4 settlements for the enforcement two-stage cluster RCT, including 1,001 disconnection-eligible compounds in the primary enforcement sample and ~608 compounds / 403 tenants in the 9-month follow-up survey).
raw_response.rationale: This empirical study (cached as the July 2021 NBER Working Paper No. 27569 version of the same title and authors) meets all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Using a two-stage cluster-randomized field experiment in Nairobi's informal settlements, it evaluates systematic contract enforcement of utility disconnection rules for bill and connection-loan nonpayment—encompassing arrears eligibility rules, formal disconnection notices, indigency/hardship exemptions and payment-plan accommodations, and physical service disconnection and reconnection—and measures direct household and compound water and sanitation access outcomes (disconnections, reconnections, piped water and pour-flush sewer connections, working connections, main water source, metered consumption, water expenditure, and fetching time) alongside administrative payment outcomes. Null statistical effects on 9-month access outcomes do not affect eligibility.
raw_response.study_design: Randomized controlled field experiments (an individual-level RCT for tenant engagement and a two-stage street-cluster RCT for disconnection contract enforcement) using administrative utility billing records and property owner/tenant surveys
